themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 99 THIS WEEK, up 700% from an 8-week average of 12.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 7.32), signaling a sudden, widespread disturbance affecting outdoor quality of life across CD208.
evidence: 99 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
700% spike with z-score of 7.32 (statistically rare event)
Park noise complaints also spiked: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 baseline (700% increase)
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden noise surge? Construction, events, street activity—ground reporting needed
Where in Riverdale/Fieldston is noise concentrated? Map 311 complaints and interview affected blocks

themes_detail.label: Animal hazard in parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-a-park complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 weekly complaints over 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score: 7.49), suggesting a concentrated wildlife or animal control issue that poses potential safety risk.
evidence: 4 animal-in-a-park complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% increase)
Z-score of 7.49 indicates statistically extreme event
Paired with unsanitary pigeon condition spike (3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 baseline, 700% increase)
reporting_angles: Which parks are affected and what animals are involved? Interview Parks Dept and residents
Is this a pigeon/rat infestation or larger wildlife? Public health implications?

themes_detail.label: Lead exposure alerts spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.4 weekly complaints (264% spike, z-score: 4.23), indicating a potential emerging public health concern in housing stock that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 5 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (264% increase, z-score: 4.23)
Lead is a health hazard particularly for children; even small spike warrants attention
Aligns with long-running CB budget priority for housing renovation/upgrade
reporting_angles: Where are the lead complaints concentrated? Are they in rentals or owner-occupied buildings?
Is this related to recent renovations (317 DOB permits filed in past 90 days) disturbing lead paint?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation service failures
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints spiked to 9 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.4 weekly (554% spike, z-score: 4.08), and street sweeping complaints hit 8 THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 baseline (814% spike, z-score: 5.23), indicating systemic garbage and street maintenance breakdown.
evidence: 9 missed collection complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (554% increase, z-score: 4.08)
8 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 baseline (814% increase, z-score: 5.23)
Unsanitary condition remains elevated in overall volume (440 complaints over 90 days, top 10)
reporting_angles: Has DSNY reduced service in CD208? Check crew schedules and staffing levels
Are collection routes or schedules disrupted? Interview residents on affected streets

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement complaints
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints hit 3 THREE WEEKS AGO, representing a 700% spike from a baseline of 0.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 3.77), though timing is slightly stale; suggests underlying street vending or regulatory issue worth monitoring for recurrence.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 3.77)
Timing is older than other spikes but remains statistically significant
Long-running CB priority on traffic/pedestrian safety may relate to street vending enforcement
reporting_angles: Is there a specific vendor problem (unlicensed food carts, street obstruction) residents reported?
Has enforcement activity increased or decreased since the spike 3 weeks ago? Follow-up needed
